econ-micro-01-c5.text: Steven A. Greenlaw, David Shapiro, Daniel MacDonald (2022). Principles of Economics 3e, 3.4 Price Ceilings and Price Floors. OpenStax.
econ-micro-01-c5.quote: Perhaps the best-known example of a price floor is the minimum wage.
econ-micro-01-c5.claim: Price ceilings (rent control) and price floors (minimum wage) lock prices off equilibrium and produce persistent shortages or surpluses.

econ-micro-02-c1.text: (2023). 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023: Full Lecture Summaries. MIT OpenCourseWare.
econ-micro-02-c1.quote: For example, if quantity demanded falls by 2% for each 1% increase in price, ϵ = −2.
econ-micro-02-c1.claim: An elasticity of 2 means a 1% price increase causes a 2% drop in quantity.

econ-micro-02-c4.text: (2023). 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023: Full Lecture Summaries. MIT OpenCourseWare.
econ-micro-02-c4.quote: Most goods are normal goods: they have a positive income elasticity. Consumption of normal goods increases as income rises.
econ-micro-02-c4.claim: If it's positive, the good is normal (most things).

econ-micro-03-c1.text: (2023). 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023: Full Lecture Summaries. MIT OpenCourseWare.
econ-micro-03-c1.quote: The important principle of diminishing marginal utility states that consumers receive less utility from each unit of a good they consume.
econ-micro-03-c1.claim: This is the law of diminishing marginal utility, and it explains why demand curves slope down.

econ-micro-04-c2.text: (2023). 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023: Full Lecture Summaries. MIT OpenCourseWare.
econ-micro-04-c2.quote: Marginal product of labor is the change in the total output resulting from using an extra unit of labor, holding other inputs constant.
econ-micro-04-c2.claim: The marginal product of an input is the extra output from one more unit, holding other inputs fixed.

econ-micro-04-c5.text: (2023). 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023: Full Lecture Summaries. MIT OpenCourseWare.
econ-micro-04-c5.quote: Increasing returns to scale: input increases proportionally, and output increases more than proportionally.
econ-micro-04-c5.claim: Increasing returns to scale: output more than doubles.

econ-micro-05-c2.text: (2023). 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023: Full Lecture Summaries. MIT OpenCourseWare.
econ-micro-05-c2.quote: Monopolist has to decrease price on all units sold in order to sell one additional unit
econ-micro-05-c2.claim: To sell more, the monopolist must drop the price, and not just on the marginal unit but on every unit.

econ-micro-05-c4.text: (2023). 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023: Full Lecture Summaries. MIT OpenCourseWare.
econ-micro-05-c4.quote: Identical Bertrand duopolists drive price down to marginal cost.
econ-micro-05-c4.claim: Surprisingly, with identical products and constant marginal cost, two firms is enough to drive price down to MC: the Bertrand paradox.

econ-micro-05-c4.text: (2023). 14.01 Principles of Microeconomics, Fall 2023: Full Lecture Summaries. MIT OpenCourseWare.
econ-micro-05-c4.quote: Cartels are fundamentally unstable (incentive to “cheat” and raise own production) and because they are illegal (antitrust laws).
econ-micro-05-c4.claim: Real oligopolies often try to coordinate (cartels, OPEC), but cooperation is fragile because each member has a strong incentive to cheat: a classic prisoner's dilemma.

econ-micro-03-c5.text: Robert T. Jensen, Nolan H. Miller (2007). Giffen Behavior: Theory and Evidence. NBER Working Paper 13243.
econ-micro-03-c5.quote: Subsidizing the prices of dietary staples for extremely poor households in two provinces of China, we find strong evidence of Giffen behavior for rice in Hunan, and weaker evidence for wheat in Gansu.
econ-micro-03-c5.claim: Jensen and Miller (2008) found Giffen behavior for rice and wheat among poor households in Hunan and Gansu, China.

econ-micro-06-c2.text: (1991). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 1991. NobelPrize.org.
econ-micro-06-c2.quote: Coase showed that every given distribution of property rights among individuals tends to be reallocated through contracts if it is to the mutual advantage of the parties and not prevented by transaction costs
econ-micro-06-c2.claim: Ronald Coase argued that if property rights are clearly defined and bargaining is costless, parties can negotiate to the efficient outcome regardless of who initially holds the right.

econ-micro-06-c4.text: (2009). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2009. NobelPrize.org.
econ-micro-06-c4.quote: Elinor Ostrom has demonstrated how common property can be successfully managed by user associations.
econ-micro-06-c4.claim: Elinor Ostrom showed that communities often self-govern common-pool resources

econ-micro-06-c5.text: (2001). Press release: The Prize in Economic Sciences 2001. NobelPrize.org.
econ-micro-06-c5.quote: The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences has decided to award the Bank of Sweden Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel, 2001, jointly to George A. Akerlof University of California at Berkeley, USA, A. Michael Spence Stanford University, USA, and Joseph E. Stiglitz Columbia University, USA
econ-micro-06-c5.claim: Spence, Akerlof, and Stiglitz shared the 2001 Nobel for working this out.
